descriptions.text: A post-audit modification for gas optimisation removed a critical line of code in the CvxRewardDistributor contract’s claimMultipleStaking function, which failed to validate the claimContracts array. This allowed the attacker to inject a malicious contract with a matching function signature claimCvgCvxMultiple, tricking the contract into minting 58 million unauthorized CVG tokens, which were then swapped for other assets. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0x636be30e58acce0629b2bf975b5c3133840cd7d41ffc3b903720c528f01c65d9 Analysis: https://blockapex.medium.com/convergence-finance-hack-analysis-7f54f8e0c4ec

Convergence Finance was attacked. 58M CVG have been minted and sold by the hacker for approximately $210,000 ( the whole portion of tokens dedicated to staking emissions); Approximately $2,000 of unclaimed rewards from Convex have also been stolen. A lack of validation in the input given by the user in the function claimMultipleStaking of the reward distribution contract is the root cause of the exploit.

On August 1, 2024, Convergence Finance was exploited via a missing input validation in its reward distributor contract, allowing an attacker to mint 58 million CVG tokens, swap them for roughly $210,000 worth of ETH and stablecoins, and move proceeds through Tornado Cash. The CvxRewardDistributor contract's claimMultipleStaking function accepted arbitrary staking contract addresses without verifying their legitimacy. This allowed a malicious contract to return inflated reward amounts, causing unauthorized minting of CVG tokens.

An attacker took advantage of a flaw in the code for the yield farming project ConvergenceFi, draining it of all the tokens that had been allocated for staking emissions. Because a function call in the smart contract did not do proper validation, an attacker was able to provide their own smart contract that set the amount of tokens to return to anything they wanted. Naturally, the attacker set it to return all 58.7 million tokens available to them, which they quickly swapped to around $210,000 and laundered through Tornado Cash. Although ConvergenceFi described itself as audited , they admitted they had made changes to that portion of the code after the audits.…
